investigations.name: 00-simulation-core
investigations.title: The Simulation Core — a composable foundation for physiological modeling
investigations.objective:
What can the simulation core do? This investigation takes ONE real model — the
BioGears sepsis core — and shows four capabilities on it, each as something you
can open and run, not a claim on a slide:
  1. COMPOSITION  — run the same spec under interchangeable engines (study 01).
  2. ENSEMBLES    — run a severity × engine batch in one orchestrated sweep (study 02).
  3. ORCHESTRATION / WORKFLOWS — compose modules into a pipeline and hand an
     Antimony/SBML file between engines (study 03).
  4. PERFORMANCE  — profile where the compute goes and how fast each engine is (study 04).
A fidelity backbone (study 05) keeps it honest: where the engines agree, and where
they do not.
investigations.claim:
The simulation core runs one sepsis specification under three interchangeable
engines: BioGears (C++ physiology), Tellurium (exact SBML via roadrunner/CVODE),
and a PyTorch surrogate. It composes and orchestrates them into workflows (including
passing an Antimony/SBML file between engines), runs them as ensembles, and does so
performantly (seconds to hours across engines; a ~40,000× surrogate tier). Every
capability below is a runnable artifact. The surrogate is a fast approximate tier —
bounded, not yet clinically accurate — not a drop-in replacement.

investigations.name: 01-composition
investigations.title: Model Interchangeability — one physiological specification, multiple implementations
investigations.objective:
Does the same sepsis specification run under interchangeable engines by swapping
one box — BioGears (C++ physiology), the exact SBML extraction (Tellurium/CVODE),
and a PyTorch surrogate — all through one typed-port interface?
investigations.claim:
The same sepsis core runs under three interchangeable engines — BioGears (C++),
Tellurium (exact SBML via roadrunner/CVODE), and a PyTorch surrogate — each a box
over the same typed observable ports. Swapping engines is swapping one box's
address. The nine-observable overlay shows the two full-physics engines (BioGears
and exact Tellurium) run the same spec and track to within ~0.1% on the inflammation
core; the surrogate is the third interchangeable engine (its speed and approximate
behavior are study 04). Where the full-physics engines diverge — the hemodynamic
layer — is the fidelity backbone (study 05).

parent_studies.rationale: Interchangeability needs the shared core and the one sepsis model.

investigations.name: 02-ensembles
investigations.title: Simulation Ensembles — systematic perturbation and comparative physiology
investigations.objective:
Can the simulation core run the sepsis model as an ENSEMBLE — many configurations
(severity × engine) executed as one orchestrated batch and gathered into a single
comparison?
investigations.claim:
The sepsis core runs as a severity {0,1,3} × engine {BioGears, Tellurium, surrogate}
ensemble, gathered into one grid. The two full-physics engines agree to within ~0.1% and
show the expected severity response (minimum tissue integrity 1.00 healthy -> 0.97
mild -> 0.24 severe); their heavy runs are cited from the committed severity studies.
The surrogate ran live across every cell in the same batch — the orchestration proof
that the harness executes many cheap configurations in one sweep — and is flagged a
fast approximate tier (its endpoint is out of physical range; its real contribution,
speed, is study 04).

parent_studies.rationale: Ensembles sweep the interchangeable spec across severity and engine.

investigations.name: 03-workflows
investigations.title: Model Orchestration — composable workflows across models, tools, and execution systems
investigations.objective:
Can the simulation core compose registered modules into a workflow and hand an
Antimony/SBML file between engines — all through a small, uniform API, with no new
simulation code?
investigations.claim:
The simulation core composes registered modules into a workflow and hands an
Antimony/SBML file between engines, using the four-verb API and no new simulation
code. The BioGears sepsis core — extracted to the portable file biogears_sepsis.ant —
is handed to the TelluriumUTCStep engine (load the file, run it), composed in one
workflow with a NeuralProcess surrogate tier and a MathExpressionStep derivation,
and run end-to-end in a few seconds. The four verbs (list -> call -> connect -> run)
are the entire surface; the portable artifact is the interface between engines.

parent_studies.rationale: Orchestration composes the interchangeable modules into a workflow.

investigations.name: 04-performance
investigations.title: Scalable Simulation — performance, acceleration, and fidelity-aware execution
investigations.objective:
How fast is the simulation core, and where does the compute go? For one matched
48 h sepsis run, what does each engine cost, what dominates that cost, and how much
does the learned surrogate save?
investigations.claim:
For one matched 48 h severe-sepsis run, the same spec spans more than 4 orders of
magnitude of compute. BioGears (C++ physiology) takes ~3.38 h. Tellurium (exact SBML
via roadrunner/CVODE) takes ~2.81 h. The PyTorch surrogate takes ~0.2 s — about
40,000x faster than the exact SBML path. The exact engines spend nearly all of that
time integrating the stiff 91-state ODE. That solve needs an implicit stiff solver
(CVODE), so a faster or Rust explicit integrator cannot speed it up; the real levers
are a better stiff solver, GPU-parallel patients, or a surrogate. The surrogate
replaces the ODE solve with one forward pass. A live per-step micro-benchmark on this
machine measures ~526 ms for one exact CVODE step of the real model against ~0.04 ms
for one surrogate forward pass — the exact per-step cost is ~13,000x the surrogate's.
The surrogate is a fast approximate tier (bounded, not yet clinically accurate), not
a drop-in replacement.

parent_studies.rationale: Performance benchmarks the interchangeable engines on the same spec.

investigations.name: 05-fidelity
investigations.title: Mechanistic Fidelity — agreement, discrepancy, and missing physiology
investigations.objective:
The capability studies show the same spec running under interchangeable engines.
But do the engines actually agree, and where do they diverge? This is the honest
backbone. The demonstration is credible only if the engines' limits are measured,
not hidden.
investigations.claim:
The engines agree where the extraction is faithful and diverge where it is not. At
rest both hold the StandardMale baseline. Under infection the inflammation core
(tissue integrity, blood pathogen) matches to within ~0.1% in both the mild and
severe arms. They diverge in the hemodynamic layer. The engine fluctuates
continuously (from its nutrition schedule and full homeostatic control) while the
autonomous extraction is near-flat. Under severe sepsis both reach MAP<65 shock, but
by opposite mechanisms and in flipped order: the engine by a hypodynamic low-output
route (MAP<65 at 69.3 h), the extraction by a hyperdynamic vasodilatory route (MAP<65
at 54.1 h) — ~15 h earlier, even though it lags ~11 h on systolic pressure. Every
divergence maps to a vasomotor, fluid, or metabolic subsystem the extraction omits
(nitric oxide, fever vasodilation, renal fluid handling, lactate, intracellular
water). The surrogate is a further, coarser approximation (study 04): fast, bounded,
not clinically accurate.

parent_studies.rationale: Fidelity tests whether the interchangeable engines actually agree; it finds the hemodynamic divergence.

investigations.name: 06-cosimulation
investigations.title: Dynamic Coupling — bidirectional co-simulation and physiological intervention
investigations.objective:
Can the simulation core run a genuine co-simulation — two processes that exchange
state on every tick inside one composite — rather than running engines in parallel
and comparing them afterwards (studies 01/02) or as parallel tiers (study 03)?
investigations.claim:
The `sepsis_cosim` composite couples two process-bigraph processes that exchange
state every tick. The Tellurium sepsis physiology engine writes its global parameters
(pathogen, hemodynamics) to a shared store. An antibiotic-PK controller process reads
the pathogen, integrates a one-compartment drug PK, and writes the drug-killed
pathogen back into the engine through its `parameters_in` port before the engine's
next step. The treatment the controller computes at tick n changes the physiology the
engine integrates at tick n+1 — a real feedback loop, not two independent runs. With
the controller enabled (closed-loop antibiotic), bacteremia is cleared. With it
disabled (treat=False, the matched control from the same composite), bacteremia
climbs. The pathogen drives septic collapse, so the loop removes the cause. The
multi-day clinical endpoint itself (studies 03/05) is beyond this run's horizon.

parent_studies.rationale: Intervention acts on the sepsis mechanism fidelity establishes (detect discrepancy -> test treatment).

investigations.name: 07-evidence
investigations.title: Scientific Evidence & Acceptance — from simulation runs to reproducible claims
investigations.objective:
Can the Workbench turn simulation outputs into traceable evidence, evaluate explicit
acceptance criteria, tell supported claims from unsupported ones, and flag the
verification still needed?
investigations.claim:
The Workbench evaluates pre-declared acceptance criteria against committed evidence
and records a traceable verdict for each. Using the study-05 severe-arm milestones as
the evidence source (evaluate_acceptance.py -> out/acceptance_eval.json), four criteria
were declared with tolerances and evaluated: INFLAM-01 (minimum tissue integrity agrees
to within 1%) passes at 0.0044% relative error; INFLAM-02 (peak blood pathogen within
1%) passes at 0.12%; HEMO-01 (time to MAP < 65 mmHg agrees within 6 h) fails at 15.3 h
apart (engine 69.3 h vs SBML 54.1 h); and SURR-01 (surrogate hemodynamic accuracy within
10% of the exact engine) is pending — its validator has not been run. Two pass, one fail,
one pending, each linked to its evidence artifact or its missing-evidence note.

parent_studies.rationale: Evaluates the fidelity discrepancy as acceptance criteria.
Evaluates the intervention evidence (discrepancy -> counterfactual -> evidence).

investigations.name: 08-reduced-model
investigations.title: Model Reduction — event-driven vs event-free (speed vs fidelity)
investigations.objective:
The per-beat event (E_beat) fires ~205k times over 48 h and is ~99% of the full
model's runtime. Can we replace the events with a continuous mean-hemodynamics model
that still reproduces the sepsis trajectory — and how much faster, and at what cost
to fidelity?
investigations.claim:
Removing the per-beat event and the pulsatile layer makes the 48 h sepsis run
~10^7-10^8x faster and closes the COPASI-vs-Tellurium gap. The event-free model
(sources/eventfree_sepsis.ant) runs a 48 h severe course in ~0.2 ms under roadrunner
and ~0.06 ms under COPASI, versus ~2.81 h (roadrunner) and ~3.7 h (COPASI) for the
full model — and with the events gone COPASI is as fast as roadrunner, because the
~3x engine gap was entirely per-event interpreter overhead. Fitted to the exact
severe arm, the reduced model tracks blood pathogen to ~10%, tissue integrity to
~4%, and the mean-MAP decline to ~4% RMSE. It trades fidelity for that speed: it
under-reaches the shock depth (MAP ~80 vs 69.5 mmHg; SVR ~0.78 vs 0.665) and, being
monotonic, misses the full model's baroreflex SVR compensation-then-decompensation,
and it has no pulsatility (no SBP/DBP pulse pressure).

parent_studies.rationale: Performance localized the cost to the per-beat event; this study removes it.
Tests how much hemodynamic fidelity is lost when the pulsatile event layer is dropped.

investigations.name: 09-event-architecture
investigations.title: Event architecture — lifting the discrete sepsis events out of the model
investigations.objective:
BioGears is event-driven, and the SBML extraction encodes that as SBML events run by
roadrunner's root-finder — opaque to the composition engine. Can we use vivarium's own
event-driven capabilities instead: lift the model's discrete events OUT of the SBML and
express them as first-class process-bigraph constructs, and still reproduce the model?
investigations.claim:
The discrete sepsis events can be lifted out of the SBML into the vivarium layer and the
hybrid still reproduces the full model — at no runtime cost versus the fastest exact option.
The event-free SBML core, driven by viva-impulse's ScheduledEvent (E_infect) and
ThresholdSwitch (E_tlrOn/Off) through the TelluriumImpulseBridge, reproduces the full
event-driven model (same proto_valve continuous core, events relocated): over a 2 h severe
run the hemodynamics (MAP, SBP, HR, SVR) agree to ~1e-4 max relative and tissue integrity to
~3e-4. Blood pathogen tracks with a brief ~20% transient during the steep infection rise
that converges to ~0.2% — the one visible residual, and it is purely the tick-quantization
of the infection start (the ScheduledEvent fires at the first 10 s tick at or after
infectionStart, versus the SBML event's exact root-find; a smaller interval shrinks it).
Runtime (same roadrunner engine + Composite harness, this machine, 2 h severity 3): full
sepsis_sbml 284 s, proto_valve 236 s, hybrid 233 s — the hybrid matches the fastest exact
option and is ~1.22x faster than the full event-driven model, because its continuous core is
event-free (no CVODE root returns) and the lifted events are cheap. So against the other run
options the event-driven format is prediction-faithful AND runtime-competitive, and it buys
explicit, swappable events (a different protocol, an added controller, retimed dosing) with
no SBML surgery — unlike the learned surrogate (study 04), which is ~1000x faster but
inadmissible on 8/9 severe observables. This holds for the SLOW, timescale-separated events
(infection onset, the TLR mode switch); the fast per-beat event stays in the engine (study
08) — and the extraction report confirms E_beat is BioGears' own per-cardiac-cycle
measurement event, intrinsic to the beat and not separable to the tick.

parent_studies.rationale: Study 08 removed the per-beat event by reduction; this study removes the remaining discrete events by RELOCATION — lifting them into the composition layer rather than approximating them away.
Cosimulation established the engine coupling channel (parameters_in writeback); this study reuses it to inject vivarium-owned discrete events into the engine.

investigations.name: 00-contract
investigations.title: The contract — simulate(model, request) → results + verification
investigations.objective:
Can one interface take any model, run it under any engine, and return both the results
and a verification that the run can be trusted?
investigations.claim:
simulate(model, request) is the simulation core's one interface: model in, results +
verification out. Four runs through the identical call (run_contract.py ->
out/contract_runs.json, chart 01) each return their observables together with a
VerificationReport — ran, finite, physical admissibility per observable, and, when a
second engine is requested, cross-engine agreement. The SBML file runs under Tellurium
and under COPASI; the same model cross-checked against COPASI agrees with Tellurium to
~1e-4; a registered composite runs through the same interface with a severity override.
Every run is self-verified; the engine is a swappable box behind the contract, and no
simulator is wrapped more than once.
